description: An interactive 3D game set on Mars, where players explore a Martian environment and follow mission objectives. The project aims to bring space exploration to life through an immersive, hands-on experience.
summary:
An interactive 3D Mars exploration game where players prepare for an expedition at a habitat base, explore on foot, and drive the Tortuga rover. The main mission involves photographing a rock outcrop and collecting a sample, while managing oxygen, water, food, rover power, and hull integrity.

A bonus mission challenges players to restore communications by choosing between cleaning a solar panel or using a limited spare battery. The game includes seismic monitoring, route selection, and a Portuguese–English language switch.
details:
Our project is an interactive 3D Mars exploration game that combines scientific fieldwork with engineering decisions and resource management. Players control an astronaut and the Tortuga rover, using a fixed habitat base to prepare equipment, replenish supplies, and begin an expedition.

The main mission, “The Red Crust,” introduces geological observation and sample collection. Players leave the rover to photograph the reddish exterior and exposed fractured face of a rock outcrop in the same frame. They then return to the rover to operate its drilling arm, collect sample M01, and seal it for transport back to the base.

A bonus mission, “Restore the Signal,” presents a choice between time and stored energy. A communication station has insufficient power because dust covers its solar panel. Players can spend 20 seconds cleaning the panel and preserve their spare battery, or consume one battery to restore power immediately. Both solutions enable data transmission, but produce different resource outcomes. The maintenance duration is a gameplay simplification.

During exploration, players monitor astronaut supplies, rover power, hull integrity, and instrument condition. A seismometer display, route options, repair controls, and evacuation mechanics provide additional operational decisions. The game distinguishes observed seismic activity from scientific interpretations: its fictional events do not represent earthquake or eruption predictions.

The application uses React, TypeScript, and PlayCanvas to combine a browser-based interface with an interactive 3D environment. Players can switch between Portuguese and English without restarting the mission.

The project connects to the Space Mission Design Game challenge by turning mission preparation, scientific objectives, and limited resources into playable decisions. Its purpose is to help players explore how equipment, time, energy, and crew safety influence the execution of a space mission.
